Table of Contents

## How Do Satellite Phones Work

Satellite phones rely on a network of satellites orbiting Earth. They connect signals from low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites directly to earth stations, handsets, or other communication devices.

Once connected, these devices send voice and data, including text messaging and Internet, at speeds as high as 9.8 kbps.

Though that may not appear like much in today’s mobile world, it’s still fast enough to send emails and share images, assuming they were reduced in size to meet the data transfer limitations of these phones.

## Where Do Satellite Phones Work Best

Satellite phones are best used in places where other types of communication, such as cellular networks, are not available or where they do not exist.

Areas on land, sea, and even air where little or no communication infrastructure is available, like on ocean cruises, in the middle of the desert, and while flying on private aircraft can use satellite phones.

## Satellite Phones are not for Everyone – Here’s Why

Satellite phones are expensive, bulky, and not as simple to use as mobile phones. Moreover, they require a direct line of sight with a LEO satellite and cannot be used indoors unless paired with a satellite Wi-Fi-Hotspot.

### Cost

For many users, the price is the main barrier to entry. Satellite phones can cost anywhere between $500 and $1,500, and often require users to pay hefty monthly fees.
